evidence.assessment: CI1 ordinary Linux runner failed at root ownership before reaching intended archive fault assertions. The ordinary fixture now substitutes privileged validation while retaining real directory types, device/inode identity, contents, rename behavior, recovery bindings, and existing service-order/no-stop checks. The read_private replacement also bypasses private-file metadata checks in this ordinary fixture; it is not evidence of real filesystem security. The root fixture does not mock those validators and adds real foreign-ownership rejection for the candidate and preparation record before service removal; existing real symlink and successful archive integration remain. No prior negative security assertion was removed.

Ordinary fixture mock is corrected from unused chown to actual fchown; serialization, endpoint-key isolation, disabled-provider omission and rejection-before-writing assertions are retained. New root test executes real publication and checks root/native-group 0640 ownership of runtime/native-env, private provider.env ownership/mode, absence of bearer in public registry, and the selected endpoint credential in native environment.

Old fake profile omitted kind and could not represent a valid saved provider, causing KeyError before redaction. Fixture now uses real Profiles.save/records for both valid legacy and multi-connection settings. Exact redaction assertion expands from two to three secrets including a disabled connection. Allowed fixed service/line-count and unrelated ssh rejection assertions remain. Production saveProfileName stores ProviderStore.read settings, not the removed incomplete mock shape.
